answer: Seats remain scarce because each one must face live neighbors. Every seat is a vertex that posts 20 unique work traces signed under its key. Each epoch the chain opens a pulse, a 12-minute live slot, and publishes a signal roster pairing every vertex with 2 random peers. Each pair runs 8 follow-up questions taken from the examinee's traces, due in 30 seconds and countersigned, so one speaker cannot cover two vertices in the same slot. 500 fakes need 10,000 genuine traces plus 500 live exams at once, even if no one later looks.
